lessons.title: Form 15G and Form 15H: Who Can Submit Them and When

body.text: Form 121 is a declaration, not a request. You are stating that your tax for the whole year will be nil, and the payer stops TDS on that promise. Get it right and your money stays with you. Get it wrong and you have made a false statement under the tax law.

children.text: Kamala, 66, a retired teacher in Coimbatore, used to lose ₹48,000 a year to TDS on her fixed deposits and then wait months for a refund. Megha, 34, a homemaker in Surat, heard from a relative that "Form 121 stops TDS" and tried to submit one at her bank, which refused it. Both have nil tax. Only one of them was eligible. This lesson explains the two tests that decide who can use Form 121, when to submit it, and why a careless declaration is risky.

markDefs.definition: A self-declaration furnished to a payer under Section 393(6) of the Income-tax Act, 2025, read with Rule 211, stating that the declarant's tax for the year will be nil so that TDS is not deducted on specified income. It replaces Forms 15G and 15H.

children.text: replaces the old Forms 15G and 15H. It is furnished under Section 393(6) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (formerly Section 197A) read with Rule 211 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026. When you give it to a payer, such as your bank, the payer does not deduct TDS on the income covered, allots the declaration a unique identification number, and reports it in its quarterly TDS statement.

points: Form 15G for individuals below 60, HUFs and other eligible non-company persons
Form 15H for resident individuals aged 60 or above
Filed under Section 197A of the 1961 Act
Two forms, two sets of conditions

Age still changes which conditions apply

body.text: Non-residents cannot use Form 121, and neither can companies or firms. It is designed for resident individuals, HUFs and similar persons whose total income is too low to be taxed.

cells: Tax on your estimated total income for the tax year, from all sources and after deductions and rebate, must be nil
The total of all income you declare in Form 121, across all payers, must not exceed the maximum amount not chargeable to tax, which is ₹4,00,000 in the new regime

children.text: The second test is why many people are caught out. In the new regime, the Section 156 rebate makes tax nil on taxable income up to ₹12,00,000. So plenty of people below 60 have nil tax on incomes of ₹6,00,000 or ₹8,00,000. But if the income they want to shield with Form 121 is above ₹4,00,000, test 2 fails and the payer should not accept the form. Senior citizens only need to pass test 1.

FD interest of ₹5,50,000, no other income
Pension of ₹3,60,000 and FD interest of ₹4,80,000
Salary of ₹14,00,000 and FD interest of ₹70,000

body.title: Quick Check: Why Was Megha Refused?
body.question: Megha, 34, earns ₹5,50,000 of FD interest and has no other income. Her tax is nil in the new regime because of the rebate. Why can she not use Form 121?
options: Homemakers are not allowed to submit Form 121
Her FD interest of ₹5,50,000 exceeds the ₹4,00,000 cap that applies to people below 60
Her tax is not really nil
Form 121 is only for senior citizens
body.explanation: She passes test 1, because her tax is nil. But test 2 requires income declared in Form 121 to stay within ₹4,00,000 for anyone below 60, and her interest is ₹5,50,000. Her bank will deduct 10%, ₹55,000, which she can claim back in full by filing her return. Had she been 60 or older, test 2 would not apply.

body.title: Try It: What Form 121 Saves Kamala
body.prompt: Kamala, 66, has a pension of ₹3,60,000 and FD interest of ₹4,80,000 from one bank. Her taxable income after the ₹75,000 standard deduction is ₹7,65,000, so her tax is nil. How much TDS does Form 121 prevent the bank from deducting this year?
body.explanation: Her interest exceeds the ₹1,00,000 senior citizen threshold, so without Form 121 the bank would deduct 10% of ₹4,80,000 = ₹48,000. As a senior citizen she only needs nil tax to qualify, so a Form 121 submitted in April keeps the full interest in her account, without waiting for a refund.

children.text: Test 1 is about your total income for the whole year, not just the income from the payer you are giving the form to. Before you sign, add up everything.

body.caption: What to include in your estimate

cells: Interest from every bank, post office and company, including accrued interest on cumulative FDs
Each bank only sees its own deposits
Retirees forget pension is taxable, students forget internship stipends
Often treated as family money rather than income
Capital gains from shares, mutual funds or property
A one-off sale later in the year can push tax above nil
Small amounts spread across many companies add up

body.text: Some income, such as capital gains taxed at special rates, may not be fully covered by the rebate. If you expect gains on shares, mutual funds or property during the year, work out the tax carefully before declaring it will be nil, or get advice.

events.title: Estimate and submit
events.description: Estimate your total income for the new tax year. If you pass both tests, submit Form 121 to each bank, company or fund that will pay you, before its first credit.

events.title: Online or at the branch
events.description: Most banks accept Form 121 through net banking or their app. You can also sign a physical form at the branch. The payer allots it a unique identification number. Keep the acknowledgement.

events.title: New deposits, new payers
events.description: Opening an FD with a new bank, or buying a new dividend stock, means submitting a fresh Form 121 to that payer.

events.title: Tell the payer
events.description: If an unexpected sale or new job means your tax will no longer be nil, inform the payers you gave Form 121 to so TDS can resume, and plan advance tax.

events.title: Start again
events.description: A Form 121 is valid only for the tax year it is given for. Submit a new one every year.

body.title: Fill in the Blank: Timing
body.textWithBlank: Form 121 should reach the payer before the income is ___, because TDS already deducted cannot be reversed by a later declaration.
body.explanation: TDS applies at the time of credit or payment, whichever is earlier. If the bank has already credited interest and deducted TDS, a Form 121 submitted afterwards only stops future deductions. The TDS already deducted must be claimed as a refund in your return.

cells: Interest on FDs, RDs, bonds and other securities
Income from mutual fund units, such as IDCW
Insurance commission and certain life insurance payouts

children.text: The Risk of a False Declaration

Form 121 carries a signed verification. Knowingly declaring nil tax when you expect to owe tax is a false statement. Under Section 482 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (formerly Section 277), that can lead to prosecution, with rigorous imprisonment of three months to two years plus a fine in ordinary cases, and up to seven years where the tax sought to be evaded exceeds ₹25 lakh. And it does not even hide the income: banks report all interest to the department, so it appears in your AIS regardless.

body.title: Scenario: Circumstances Change in November
body.scenario: Deepak, 58, a retired army officer in Dehradun, submitted Form 121 to his bank in April 2026. At the time, his pension and FD interest put his tax at nil and his declared interest at ₹3,00,000, within the cap. In November he sells an inherited plot and makes a long-term capital gain of ₹18,00,000.
body.prompt: Was his declaration false? What should he do now?
body.modelAnswer: His declaration was honest when he made it, because he genuinely expected nil tax. But his tax for the year will no longer be nil, since a gain of ₹18,00,000 will attract capital gains tax. He should promptly inform his bank in writing that his Form 121 no longer holds, so it can deduct TDS on interest credited from now on. More importantly, he should work out the tax on the capital gain and pay advance tax in the remaining instalments, or as soon as possible, to limit interest. When filing his return, he reports all interest and the capital gain. Acting quickly shows good faith. Leaving the declaration in place while knowing it is wrong is what turns a changed circumstance into a false statement.

body.title: Before You Sign Form 121
steps: Estimate total income for the tax year from every source, including accrued interest and expected capital gains
Confirm your tax on that income will be nil after deductions and rebate
If you are below 60, add up all the income you plan to declare across payers and confirm it stays within ₹4,00,000
Submit to each bank, company or fund before its first credit of the year, and save the acknowledgement or UIN
Set a reminder to review your estimate mid-year, and tell payers promptly if your tax will no longer be nil
If you do not qualify, let TDS be deducted and claim the refund by filing your return

cards.definition: Declaration that tax for the year will be nil, so payers do not deduct TDS. Replaces Forms 15G and 15H from tax year 2026-27.
Provision allowing Form 121 declarations and setting the eligibility tests. Formerly Section 197A.
Tax on estimated total income from all sources, after deductions and rebate, must be nil. Applies to everyone.
For those below 60, total income declared in Form 121 must not exceed the maximum amount not chargeable to tax.
Unique identification number the payer allots to each Form 121 it receives, used when reporting it.
Prosecution for false statements in a verification, including a false Form 121. Formerly Section 277.

points: Form 121 replaced Forms 15G and 15H from tax year 2026-27, under Section 393(6) read with Rule 211
Everyone must pass the nil tax test on estimated total income from all sources
People below 60 must also keep the total income declared in Form 121 within ₹4,00,000, even if the rebate makes their tax nil
Senior citizens only need nil tax, so they can shield larger interest amounts
Submit to every payer before the first credit of the year, renew each April, and tell payers if your tax will no longer be nil
A knowingly false declaration is a prosecutable offence under Section 482, formerly 277, and the income is reported in AIS anyway

body.text: This lesson is for educational purposes only and does not constitute tax, legal or investment advice. Names and amounts are illustrative, and examples assume residents using the new regime. Eligibility conditions and limits reflect the position understood at the time of writing and can change. Verify current rules on the Income Tax Department website or consult a qualified chartered accountant before submitting a declaration.
